title: The Outlook for US Housing in 2027 amid Rising Mortgage Rates - Goldman Sachs
content: We harness every resource, insight, relationship, and competitive advantage to drive superior results for our clients. Goldman Sachs’ weekly newsletter, offering economic and markets analysis from across the firm. Subscribe now. We invest the power of Goldman Sachs' financial and intellectual capital to advance enduring economic growth and opportunity. Rising mortgage rates are likely to outweigh a longstanding housing shortage in the US next year, leading to a drop in both the sales of existing homes and the construction of new ones, according to Goldman Sachs Research. “In 2027, we expect the headwind from affordability to increasingly dominate, weighing further on activity,” economists Ronnie Walker and David Mericle write in a report. They project that existing home sales will total just 3.9 million in 2027, modestly below their forecast of 4 million for 2026 but 26% below 2019 levels. Against the backdrop of slower home sales, they forecast another year of “anemic” home price growth: 0.8% December-over-December in 2027 after 1.1% in 2026 and 1.2% in 2025. Borrowing costs are a key component of housing affordability. This year’s jump in mortgage rates—in response to the Iran War, higher oil prices, and the prospect of rate hikes by the Federal Reserve—has reduced incentives for homeowners to sell. More than 95% of mortgage borrowers have interest rates below current market rates, and 65% have rates two percentage points below market rates, creating a “lock-in” effect that is slowing sales. In order to purchase a new home, such homebuyers would need to prepay their current mortgage and take out a new mortgage at a higher rate. “The combination of mortgage borrowers refinancing at low rates en masse in 2020 and 2021 and the high current level of mortgage rates has created a significant financial cost to moving,” Walker and Mericle write. Rates for 30-year mortgages in the US have climbed to 7.32% (as of October 22). Goldman Sachs Research’s credit strategists expect mortgage rates to decline in 2027 but remain elevated at 6.4%. Even if that decline is realized, affordability will remain at historically poor levels. Beyond next year, Goldman Sachs Research expects existing home sales to gradually edge higher, reflecting the natural decay of the lock-in effect that comes from, for example, borrowers paying down their mortgages. The renewed popularity of adjustable-rate mortgages in the post-pandemic period could theoretically accelerate this process as well. As rates on such mortgages reset, they tend to erode the impact of the lock-in effect, as seen in other countries where adjustable-rate mortgages are more prevalent. But that impact is likely to be modest in the US, especially over the next couple of years. Adjustable-rate mortgages represent less than 10% of all outstanding mortgages in the US, and only a small share of them will begin to reset in the coming years. Housing activity as measured by residential fixed investment (RFI)—a component of gross domestic product that includes new home construction—is likely to begin recovering by next summer after an expected decline in the months ahead. After posting an estimated 3.1% annualized increase in this year’s third quarter, RFI is forecast to contract by 2.5%, 4%, and 1% annualized in the three quarters that follow, respectively. Thereafter, our researchers expect activity to rebound to a 1-2% growth pace starting in the second half of next year, reflecting the impact of declining mortgage rates. If rates remain at current levels instead, that would lower their RFI growth forecasts by one to two percentage points through the end of 2027. The longstanding housing shortage has kept single-family homebuilding resistant to higher interest rates. Single-family starts have averaged 3% higher than above 2019 levels despite mortgage rates that are three-and-a-half percentage points higher today. This year, however, they have declined by 3% compared with last year, and the slippage is likely to continue. Goldman Sachs Research expects single-family starts to total 0.87 million in 2027 compared to an estimated 0.90 million in 2026. Our economists point to the increase in the available supply of housing, as well as the corresponding compression of margins for homebuilders back to pre-pandemic levels. The elevated pace of homebuilding in recent years has eased historically tight supply-and-demand balances. When the available supply of housing improves, it tends to increase homebuilders’ sensitivity to affordability constraints. Prior analysis by Goldman Sachs Research shows that the higher the vacancy rate was the year before, the more sensitive housing starts are to mortgage rate increases. The combination of still-solid supply growth and slightly weaker demand should push the homeowner vacancy rate higher in the months ahead, from 1.2% in this year’s second quarter to 1.4% by the fourth quarter of 2027. Housing demand is being buoyed by domestic demographic trends that remain supportive, along with real income growth that is likely to accelerate next year, and “build-to-rent” housing, which typically involves a partnership between single-family rental companies and homebuilders to construct rental homes. But on the negative side, survey-based measures of purchase intentions have declined in recent months. Our economists also expect that reduced immigration will continue to weigh on household formation. “We expect housing demand to remain tepid,” Walker and Mericle write. title: V-League Season Opens October 31 With Men’s and Women’s Matches - 조선일보
content: Men's division rivalry between Korea Air Lines and Hyundai Capital; women's champions GS Caltex face new FIVB line-in rules The 2026-2027 V-League season, the crown jewel of winter sports, kicks off with men’s division matches between Korea Air Lines and Hyundai Capital and women’s division matches between GS Caltex and Korea Expressway Corporation on October 31, marking the start of a six-month marathon. The men’s division is expected to revolve around a two-horse race between last season’s championship rivals Korea Air Lines and Hyundai Capital, with the remaining five teams vying for supremacy. Korea Air Lines retains key players Han Seon-su, Jeong Ji-seok, and Im Dong-hyuk, while Hyundai Capital has secured Heo Su-bong and Hwang Seung-bin to anchor its core lineup. Korea Electric Power, bolstered by setter Lee Min-kyu, Asian quota player Usman (Pakistan), and foreign recruit Shaw (Canada), is poised as a potential challenger. Samsung Fire & Marine Insurance and KB Insurance’s campaigns also draw attention. Samsung has appointed Tommi Tiilikainen (Finland), the coach who led Korea Air Lines to three consecutive titles, as its new head coach. KB Insurance will be guided by Isanay Ramos (Brazil), former head coach of the South Korean men’s national team. In the women’s division, a fierce battle is anticipated despite GS Caltex’s slight edge as the reigning champions and cup winners. GS Caltex, featuring Cuban star Silva and Thai sensation Tanacha, faces challenges from Korea Expressway Corporation, which boasts Cameroonian power hitter Moma and Park Jeong-ah; Jung Ho-young and Pyo Seung-ju-led Heungkuk Life Greens; and Hyundai Engineering & Construction, which signed Mega (Indonesia) to fill the void left by retired star Yang Hyo-jin and reignite the Jung Kwan Jang phenomenon that dominated from 2023 to 2025. The Korea Volleyball Federation has adopted the FIVB’s global regulations for line in/out rulings starting this season. Replacing the previous complex local rules, any contact between the ball and the line at the moment it touches the floor will now be judged as “in.”

title: This Used Lexus Has A 467-HP V8 And Costs Half Of Its Original MSRP - Top Speed
content: You wouldn’t know it by their current lineup, but Lexus used to be the king of sedans. They actually started their brand with a full-size luxury limousine, the Lexus LS. Then, dealers called on Lexus to give them a slightly more accessible, reasonably priced sedan. Lexus responded with the ES. Then, in 1991, Toyota wanted a luxury sedan similar to Italian luxury sedans for their domestic market in Japan. It was originally dubbed the Toyota Aristo. It was such a hit that by 1993, it moved to selling internationally with a name badge switch to the GS 300. By the early to mid-2010s, the Lexus GS had already hit icon status and was a cult hit among auto enthusiasts. From the start, it was available with either a six-cylinder or a more powerful V8 engine. While there doesn’t seem to be any announced new version of the now venerated GS coming back anytime soon, there is still a lot of interest in the used market. While things are heading in the direction of electrification and turbocharged power, the GS still offers analog capabilities that the market is still looking for. We’re going to go over the necessary things to look out for if you’re interested in this future classic. First and foremost, the Lexus GS F is a luxury sedan. We already know that. The GS F is not only luxurious but also a powerful brute, predicated on its now nearly extinct powertrain. While the United States market only received an inline six-cylinder engine that made 220 horsepower, the rest of the world was already getting the V8. We received the first generation V8 here by 1998. These, however, were just regular luxury sedans with a big V8. They weren't necessarily "F" standard and didn't have any of the performance features you would come to expect. The second generation was the first Lexus GS to technically get the “F” treatment, even if it wasn’t referred to as such. That moniker belongs to the 2016 model and later. You could still get a V8 in the GS 460 from 2008 to 2011, but it wasn’t nearly as powerful. The 2016 to 2020 model is where the true power lies, as it’s tied to a massive naturally aspirated 5.0-liter V8 that outputs an impressive 467 horsepower and 389 pound-feet of torque. Even more impressive is its reported zero to 60 MPH time of just 4.4 seconds. This is also a high-revving engine that can achieve 7,100 RPM. The Lexus “F” badge on any Lexus represents the legendary Fuji Speedway in Japan. With that in mind, Lexus pulls out all the technological stops to give it the best quality sport handling you would come to expect from a mid-size sport limo. Tethered to the V8 is an eight-speed Sport Direct Shift automatic transmission that also has a manual mode. As you’d probably expect, this also has RWD, but what you might not expect is that it’s equipped with a torque vectoring differential. This allows you to choose from Standard, Slalom, and Track modes. Finally, there are Brembo brakes, a multi-link rear suspension with adaptive dampers, and a double wishbone suspension. Music to our ears. Typically, within the first five years of any mid-size luxury sedan, they lose between 45 and 60 percent of their original MSRP value. Basic economics suggest that the market just doesn’t want mid-size luxury sedans. Everybody wants an SUV, in the US at least. It's even evident in the fact that Mercedes-AMG just released their first-ever GT SUV. Sport variants of any vehicle typically hold their value slightly more than their standard counterparts, but the market is still not entirely there for luxury sedans. You would, however, be shocked to see how well the GS F holds its value. While other sedans are losing their value at a steep decline in five years, a 2016 model, for example, still retains about 44 percent of its original value, according to Kelley Blue Book. The 2018 and 2020 models aren’t that far off either, with 2018 at 48 and 2020 at 55 percent respectively. If we were to follow that same order, the original MSRPs were $85,345 to $86,035 max. Now, they're valued between $41,800 and $47,100 depending on the year, mileage, condition, and the like. It’s ended up (in the American market at least) mainly competing with the likes of the BMW M5 and Mercedes-AMG E63. Other competitors for the regular sedan include the Audi A6. If we’re talking pricing, Kelley Blue Book puts the 2018 BMW M5 at about $41,500 give or take. The AMG E63 of the same year is around $57,770, even closer to $49,000. Both the Mercedes and the BMW have more power and better traction with all-wheel drive, but the Lexus GS F has a naturally aspirated 5.0-liter V8 that most enthusiasts want. Most enthusiasts want that 5.0-liter naturally aspirated V8 because of the simplicity it offers from a maintenance standpoint. Not only that, but at the end of the day, it is considered a Toyota and is often viewed as more reliable from a maintenance standpoint. Not to take away from the Lexus brand itself, because as a standalone, it has achieved the number one spot on JD Power’s most reliable brand list for years and years. At the end of the day, however, this is still a sport sedan, and you will have to pay Sport Sedan pricing for maintenance. Repair pal suggests that the Lexus GS F shows an annual maintenance cost of around $499. This, of course, is dependent on how much you drive it, or whether you actually end up tracking it, as performance tires are often more expensive. That number of $499 also seems awfully low considering this is a more special edition than your standard model. This thing is also heavy at a curb weight of 4,034 pounds. That means you'll be changing the Brembo brakes more frequently. Be sure to ask wherever you're buying this from for a complete maintenance history, especially regarding oil changes and spark plug replacements.​​​​​​​ Although this might be a Lexus, that doesn’t mean that it comes without issues. There was a fuel pump recall for the 2016 to 2018 models, so be sure to check the VIN to confirm whether the recall was addressed or whether it affected that specific model at all. Some blog websites have reported that the carbon fiber trim has lost some of its clear coat as well. The price points for this specific model can vary wildly. You also shouldn’t necessarily buy the newest and lowest mileage one, as maintenance plays a huge role in the quality of your GS F. We’ve even seen some on Cars.com that are going for $70,000 to $90,000. If you find a model in that price range, you could also opt for the newer IS 500, which also has a 5.0-liter naturally aspirated V8. However, you might not necessarily want that, as the cabin is much more cramped. The Lexus GS offers more space, comfort, and convenience. We want to hear from you. title: “I’ll Believe Gen.G Can Win the Trophy When I See It” — League of Legends Caster Nymaera on Gen.G’s Title Chances - WIN.GG
content:
On October 22, Naerlyn Théophile met up with LPL and general League of Legends caster Alex “Nymaera” Hapgood for an exclusive WIN.gg interview. As one of the most knowledgeable people when it comes to the Chinese league, Nymaera weighed on what to expect at the ongoing LoL Worlds 2026. Favorites, dark horses, Gen.G’s curse, the LPL’s chances against the LCK: the 30-year-old Brit gave his view on them all. Alex “Nymaera” Hapgood:
Can and will are two very different questions.
Can the LPL win the World Championship?
Yes, of course. I think that they’ve shown they have the quality. In terms of the will, I get a little bit more leery of that. I think there are teams with the quality to win Worlds, particularly AL and BLG. IG, I’m a little bit more cold on. I think that they do have a good ceiling, but I’m just not sure they can consistently hit it. I think they can [win Worlds]. It is much harder to go through a whole set of LCK teams though, which seem like they’re actually ramping up quite well for Worlds. Naerlyn: Will Gen.G once again lose before the finals? Nymaera:
I don’t think the meta is shifting in any crazy way right now. And typically, Gen.G have not been as able to react to changes in the Worlds meta as well as T1. That’s been the biggest thing which held them back. I think that on paper, Gen.G are the best performing team heading into Worlds. But I don’t think they have the strongest jungle support. Naerlyn: Are Gen.G
favorites?
Do they fall to the curse? Nymaera:
I think the meta is changing less than it did in previous years. But this misses the context of some other teams being able to lock into the Worlds patch as well. I think it would be a disservice to say that they aren’t the best team heading into Worlds though. The curse though, it is one of those “I’ll believe it when I see it” when they finally reach that trophy. Naerlyn: Can TES have a respectable performance even with 369? Nymaera:
If Top Esports turned up with their main roster, I would have said much like the Gen.G case, I’ll believe it when I see it. My analyst brain has to tell me one thing, but then actually my lived experience has to tell me another thing watching these damn teams. I don’t think Top Esports with any kind of international expectations on them is a good team. They’ve just consistently failed time and time again. I wonder though, with 369 slotting in instead of ZUIAN, whether expectations are already so low that it doesn’t matter anymore. I think that ZUIAN is a very good laning player and I think he’s done very well for a younger player. 369 is less of a laning player. He’s much more of a team fighter. But I think in this kind of meta, you can’t afford to get destroyed in an individual 1v1. So, I think Top Esports might actually mental collapse less, but I think that their ceiling is so much lower with 369 coming back without any practice. Naerlyn: Who’s going to win worlds as your heart’s answer, and why? Nymaera:
My heart’s answer is BLG and if you want the real fairy tale scenario, it’s
BLG beating T1 on their way to Worlds
and returning the favor for 2024, stopping the potential four-peat as well. I think LPL would really need that shot in the arm and I think BLG giving Knight a world trophy, Viper a second world trophy for him as well it would be a very sweet experience. Naerlyn: And giving T1 the first ever loss to the LPL at Worlds in the best of five along the way. Nymaera:
Oh, they’ve done it enough at MSI, surely they can do it at Worlds, right? Naerlyn: What’s your percentage chance for that? For that scenario? With the tournament running  to the grand final on November 14, our guide shows you

title: GS Engineering & Construction Apartment Data Breach Exposes Resident Info - 조선일보
content: Cyberattack on reservation system leaks names, addresses, passwords; company advises password changes Amid growing public anxiety over a series of hacking incidents across industries such as telecommunications and finance, a data breach occurred at an apartment complex built by GS Engineering & Construction, exposing residents’ personal information to an external cyberattack. GS Engineering & Construction stated on the 30th, “We confirmed the leakage of personal information due to unauthorized external access to the apartment community facility reservation management system and have sent notices and apologies to customers.” The hacking was identified on the 28th at approximately 11:29 p.m., when GS Engineering & Construction detected signs of unauthorized account access to the reservation system. The initial unauthorized access was traced to around 10:15 a.m. the same day. The company immediately blocked external access upon detecting the breach and is currently conducting a detailed investigation into the scope and extent of the leaked information per customer. Suspected leaked data includes customers’ names, genders, dates of birth, mobile phone numbers, email addresses, residential addresses, and reservation system passwords. Given that many users reuse passwords across multiple online platforms, additional damage from password leaks is also a concern. GS Engineering & Construction advised, “We recommend changing passwords for other websites where the same password is used.” Resident registration numbers, account details, and financial information such as credit card numbers were not collected in the first place.

title: GS E&C Reports Data Breach at Xi Apartment Community System - Seoul Economic Daily
content:
Scale of Damage and Extent of Exposure by Customer Still Under Review
"We Sincerely Apologize and Will Strengthen Our Protection Systems" GS E&C (006360.KS) said personal data may have been exposed after an unauthorized outside party gained access to the reservation management system for community facilities at its Xi apartment complexes. The company said on the 30th that it detected signs of abnormal access to the system, formerly known as FMCS, at about 11:29 p.m. on the 28th. A subsequent review of access logs confirmed that unauthorized external access had occurred at about 10:15 p.m. the same day. Information that may have been exposed includes residents' names, nicknames, dates of birth, mobile phone numbers, gender, email addresses, home addresses, membership numbers, residence type, passwords, administrator IDs, head-of-household status, membership registration dates, the IP address of their last login and RF card numbers. GS E&C said the information actually exposed differs from customer to customer. The company plans to inform users of the exact items exposed and how to check whether they were affected once it completes a review of what was exposed for each customer. Passwords were stored using one-way encryption and cannot be decrypted, the company said. Unique identifying information such as resident registration numbers, as well as financial data including bank account and card numbers, were not collected or stored and therefore were not among the exposed data. "We sincerely apologize for the concern and inconvenience caused to our customers by this personal data breach," GS E&C said. "We will further strengthen our personal data protection framework and security standards to prevent a recurrence." Original reporting by Kang Do-rim for Seoul Economic Daily. title: Personal information of GS E&C apartment residents leaked; “Scale of damage being assessed” - 매일경제
content:
Some personal information belonging to residents of GS E&C apartments was leaked. On the 30th, GS E&C apologized, saying, “We confirmed that personal information had been leaked due to unauthorized external access,” and, “We sincerely apologize for causing concern.” GS E&C first detected abnormal external access on the 28th. After blocking the access and carefully analyzing the logs, it confirmed that unauthorized external access had occurred. The company said it is currently investigating in detail whether users’ personal information was leaked and, if so, the scope of the leak. The information potentially exposed includes names, nicknames, dates of birth, mobile phone numbers, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, membership numbers, residence types, passwords, and whether a person is the head of their household. GS E&C said, “Immediately upon becoming aware of the incident, we completed emergency measures, including blocking external IP addresses, implementing security policies, and reporting it to the relevant authorities, and are preparing measures to prevent a recurrence.” It added, “Please be cautious of smishing, voice phishing, and requests for personal information. We recommend changing your current passwords, including passwords for other websites where you use the same password.” GS E&C said it is working to determine the exact scale of the damage. It is currently sending notification text messages to residents who may have been affected. title: Emro to Build AI Procurement Automation Agent for GS Caltex - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media
content: Emro will build an artificial intelligence (AI) agent to automate small-value materials procurement at GS Caltex. Emro, an AI-based supply chain management software company, said on Oct. 29 that it had won a contract to develop a procurement automation AI agent for GS Caltex. The project focuses on automating approximately 2,700 small-value materials purchases handled by GS Caltex annually. The system will enable an AI agent to analyze purchase requests and carry out the entire procurement process, from requesting and evaluating quotations to selecting suppliers and issuing purchase orders. GS Caltex has been evaluating technologies to improve the efficiency of small-value procurement, led by its strategic procurement division and internal Digital and AI Transformation (DAX) Center. The company aims to automate repetitive procurement tasks, reduce employees' workloads and improve the objectivity of purchasing decisions and operational transparency. Emro will first analyze and standardize GS Caltex's historical procurement data to establish criteria for item categories, purchase amounts, procurement types, supplier selection and exception handling. Based on these criteria, the AI agent will assess whether incoming purchase requests can be automated and handle eligible transactions from quotation requests through purchase order issuance. Cases requiring additional review will be referred to procurement personnel for manual processing. Emro will also establish a monitoring system that allows procurement personnel to track the AI agent's processes and results in real time. Employees will be able to intervene when exceptions or errors occur, reducing operational risks associated with automation. The project will use Emro's proprietary AI agent development platform, AI Studio. The platform enables companies to develop, deploy and manage AI agents that integrate with internal enterprise systems to perform procurement tasks. Emro plans to integrate the AI agent with GS Caltex's existing procurement systems and support the future expansion of AI agent applications beyond small-value materials purchases to other procurement operations.

title: SHAD Unveils Terra Crash Bars for BMW R 1300 GS - BikeWale
content: SHAD Terra crash bars for the BMW R 1300 GS are set to make their show debut at EICMA 2026. This is an important expansion of the Spanish accessory maker’s adventure-focused Terra range. Until now Terra has largely been associated with panniers, top boxes and soft luggage. The addition of motorcycle protection takes the range into a new category and SHAD has chosen one of the most established large adventure motorcycles as its first application. There’s two separate protection systems for the BMW R 1300 GS. Upper Crash Bars are designed to protect the fuel tank, radiator and upper bodywork. The Lower Crash Bars concentrate on the engine, crankcase or oil sump area and exhaust headers. This modular arrangement is useful because owners can choose the degree of protection they need. Although the upper bars require the corresponding lower crash bars to be installed first. Both assemblies are made from AISI 304 stainless steel. SHAD uses 25mm-diameter tubing with a 2mm wall thickness, with the structure designed to provide high strength without adding unnecessary width around the motorcycle. The bars mount directly to the R 1300 GS’ existing chassis mounting points, meaning installation does not require cutting or drilling the motorcycle. You can pick between two finishes. The silver version uses a sandblasted and electropolished finish intended to improve corrosion resistance and the black version receives a heat-cured powder coating designed to resist abrasion and stone impacts. SHAD has also integrated the new guards with its existing Terra luggage ecosystem. The upper bars can be used as mounting points for the TR08 waterproof crash-bar bags, which add eight litres of storage on each compatible mounting position and have a maximum recommended load of 2.6kg. The TR08 uses a universal strap system and carries an IPX4 water-resistance rating. Pricing has now appeared on SHAD’s official European configurator ahead of the EICMA display. The Lower Crash Bars are listed at €283.88 and the Upper Crash Bars cost €285.88, black or silver. The question now is whether this equities boom can keep powering the firm forward. Goldman Sachs is a leading global financial institution offering advisory, underwriting, trading, asset management, and wealth management services to corporations, governments, institutions, and individuals. The firm is renowned for its role in mergers, capital raising, and market-making across stocks, bonds, currencies, and commodities. As a closely watched  financial stock, Goldman Sachs is often viewed as a real-time gauge of dealmaking, trading activity, and private markets momentum. Goldman Sachs' net revenues rose sharply compared with the same quarter last year, though they declined meaningfully from the prior quarter. Net results followed a similar pattern, climbing strongly year over year while easing sequentially. Diluted  earnings per share reflected that strength versus last year. The stock moved higher in early trading after the report before giving back some of its advance as the market digested the details. The equities business was the clear star of the quarter, with revenue rising dramatically compared with a year earlier. Growth came primarily from prime brokerage and portfolio financing, along with derivatives activity. Hedge funds and other clients have been using more leverage and more complex options structures as equity markets have stayed buoyant. Goldman's dominant position in serving these clients allowed it to capture a significant share of that activity. Prime brokerage involves lending money and securities to hedge funds and providing them with trading, clearing, and custody services. When hedge funds increase their leverage, they borrow more from firms like Goldman, generating financing revenue. These balances can provide steady income as long as client activity remains elevated. Goldman's strength in prime brokerage gives it a durable revenue source that can support results even when other trading areas slow. Fixed income, currencies, and commodities trading revenue was roughly flat compared with a year earlier but fell sharply from the prior quarter. Intermediation revenue declined in mortgages, credit, and interest rate products, partly offset by stronger activity in currencies and commodities. Financing revenue rose on mortgages and structured lending. That mixed performance shows how trading conditions can vary widely across asset classes from one quarter to the next. Goldman's Platform Solutions segment saw results decline, mainly because of markdowns on its consumer credit card loan portfolio. The firm reclassified that portfolio ahead of a planned exit from the card partnership, requiring it to adjust the portfolio's carrying value. Goldman has been steadily retreating from consumer banking to refocus on its core strengths in global banking, markets, and asset management, and these markdowns reflect the cost of that strategic shift. Goldman's standardized common equity capital ratio dipped slightly from the prior quarter, while its ratio under the advanced approach remained unchanged. The supplementary leverage ratio and its pool of core liquid assets both stayed solid. Strong capital levels give Goldman flexibility to support client activity, absorb market swings, and return capital to owners through dividends and other distributions over time. Goldman Sachs pays a regular quarterly dividend, and its  dividend yield reflects the firm's steady cash generation and capital strength. Large banks typically balance dividend payments with other capital returns based on regulatory requirements and business needs. Goldman's solid capital position supports its ability to continue rewarding owners, though future distributions will depend partly on how capital rules evolve. The first major question going forward is the durability of equities financing. If client balances remain high and lending spreads stay stable, this business could continue supporting overall results even if derivatives activity cools. However, a sharp market decline could prompt hedge funds to reduce leverage, shrinking financing balances. Monitoring client positioning and market sentiment will be essential for gauging the sustainability of this strength. Advisory and underwriting remain central to Goldman's identity. Backlog commentary will reveal how many mergers and capital-raising deals are in the pipeline. The health of the initial public offering market will also matter, since new listings generate significant underwriting fees. A reopening of the IPO window and steady merger activity could provide meaningful support for Goldman's banking revenue in coming quarters. Credit quality represents another area to watch, particularly provisions related to wholesale lending. Rising provisions could signal stress among corporate borrowers. Regulation is also in play, as proposed changes to capital rules could alter how large banks calculate risk-weighted assets and leverage ratios. Those changes could affect how much surplus capital Goldman can distribute, influencing future dividends and capital returns. The clearest risk is that equity market volatility or a downturn reduces trading activity and client leverage, slowing the equities business. Fixed income trading may remain uneven. A slowdown in dealmaking could weigh on advisory and underwriting fees. Further consumer portfolio adjustments could pressure results. And stricter capital rules could limit the firm's flexibility to return capital to owners. GS Engineering & Construction announced on the 30th that its consolidated operating profit in the third quarter of this year was tentatively counted at 95.5 billion won, down 35.7% from the same period last year. title: Dissolve GCC council if you want to ignore elected reps: Mayor R Priya - The New Indian Express
content: CHENNAI: “Ungaluku ellam oru prachanai na indha MLA kita varringa, enake oru prachanai na naan yaar kita poven?” A popular Tamil film comedy dialogue that roughly translates to “When you have a problem, you come to this MLA, when I have a problem, who do I go to?” found an unlikely parallel in the Chennai Corporation council meeting on Thursday, when Mayor R Priya said she, too, was being left out of the loop by government officials. The exchange began with councillors complaining that officials were failing to invite them to inaugurations and inspections, many of which were attended by TVK MLAs or ministers. Priya said she was facing the same problem, citing the lack of communication about Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay’s visit timings. “You’re all saying officials aren’t calling you for inaugurations or other events, but the truth is I’m in the same situation,” she said. Deputy Mayor M Magesh Kumaar said that the Mayor went to meet PM as the timings were informed but was not the case with CM. Priya said, “If the CM is coming, will I just sit in Ripon Buildings from morning to night? They have to tell me the CM’s arrival time for me to be present, which has not been communicated at all. It is not me ignoring the government, but the government ignoring the mayor.” Shr questioned why councillors were being ignored. The discussion also touched on the format prescribed by the directorate of information and public relations for plaques at inaugurated projects, with councillors objecting to it, reiterating the sidelining of elected representatives. She also said that the state could dissolve the council if it wants to sideline elected representatives. The GCC commissioner, G S Sameeran, agreed that elected representatives should be invited to such events, except during surprise inspections. title: GS Group Hackathon: 900+ Solve Field Challenges with AI - 조선일보
content: Generative AI solutions developed for real-world operational issues at 5th annual event GS Group has positioned artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies alongside eco-friendliness as the twin pillars of its future innovation strategy, accelerating AI transformation centered on field operations. The plan involves integrating AI technology into traditional core businesses to restructure competitive advantages. GS Group holds an annual Silicon Valley-style idea competition, the "GS Group Hackathon," to spread a culture of AI innovation across the group. Employees from all affiliates participate, developing solutions that apply AI to solve real-world challenges on-site. ◇900+ People Gather to Solve Field Challenges with AI The 5th GS Group Hackathon, held in September at the Westin Seoul Parnas in Gangnam-gu, Seoul, focused on the theme "‘Play with GenAI’ Season 3: Build & Act." This emphasized creating functional AI-driven results for immediate application in work and business operations, rather than merely proposing ideas. The event drew 923 participants, including 797 GS affiliates employees and 126 external participants. Over 1.5 days, participants defined problems, derived solutions, and built initial generative AI-based services. They tackled tasks using "AI-ready data"—refined datasets that AI can instantly learn and analyze. Raw data from business sites like power plants and convenience stores often lack standardized formats, making processing time-consuming. To address this bottleneck, GS has systematically refined data accumulated across its diverse operations. The internal innovation team "52g" has organized tacit knowledge, such as the expertise of skilled workers at GS Donghae Power, into AI-readable formats. They are also developing a "power plant-specific model" that understands on-site workflows. GS plans to leverage this foundation to create industry-tailored AI solutions. The GS Group Hackathon has evolved with technological and operational changes. Launched in 2022 as a digital problem-solving event, it began integrating generative AI in 2024 and opened to external companies in 2025. Cumulative participation since its inception reaches 2,732 people. ◇GS Caltex Optimizes Processes with In-House AI Development Affiliates are also driving AI-driven innovation. GS Caltex is advancing operational transformation through "Digital & AI Transformation (DAX)," which integrates digital and AI transitions. At its Yeosu plant, the company developed in-house AI models to optimize production processes using vast operational data. Previously reliant on workers’ expertise to address process anomalies, the AI now detects early signs of issues and provides real-time solutions. GS Engineering & Construction fosters a culture of free AI use among employees. It became the first domestic construction company to adopt OpenAI’s enterprise AI solution, "ChatGPT Enterprise." Additionally, the company holds an "AI Recipe" competition to enhance employees’ AI proficiency. GS Retail promotes field-centric AI transformation. It established a system to analyze customer feedback (VOC) from convenience stores, home shopping, and supermarkets using generative AI, identifying improvement tasks. The company also formed "AX Cells" to empower field staff with generative AI tools for projects like redesigning the "Franchisee Information Sharing System," which provides tailored data to convenience store owners. Training, workshops, and AI platforms are provided to support this initiative.

title: Veterans Ministry, GS Retail to Install QR Signs at Independence Fighters' Graves - Seoul Economic Daily
content: The Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs said on the 29th that it signed a social contribution agreement with GS Retail (007070) at the National Museum of Korean Provisional Government to promote a culture of honoring national merit. Under the agreement, the two organizations will install smart information boards at scattered graves of independence fighters, allowing visitors to view the achievements of the deceased and historical records of the independence movement through QR codes. The project aims to inform the public of the merits of those who fought for the country. They will also step up practical support, including cleanup and maintenance work at burial sites and donations of goods to people of national merit and their families. Marking the 81st anniversary of National Liberation Day this year, the ministry launched its first "See Independence Fighters Up Close" project, funded through the citizen participatory budget, to install smart information boards and provide information on independence fighters buried outside national cemeteries. Of the roughly 3,000 graves of independence fighters scattered across the country, about 50 were selected for installation based on the level of decoration — the Order of Merit for National Foundation, Independence Medal or higher — and regional balance. The ministry and GS Retail plan to install smart information boards at 18 additional graves beyond those 50 and to continue cooperating in the future. "The ministry will actively pursue partnerships with a wide range of companies so that gratitude and respect for the sacrifice and devotion of independence fighters and people of national merit can spread throughout society," Minister Kwon O-eul said. Georgia Southern University researchers can now compete for federal funding, including Department of Defense funding that requires strict cybersecurity protections, after the university’s Talon Secure virtual environment earned Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Level 2 certification. With Talon Secure certified, Georgia Southern faculty can pursue larger grants, support current Department of Defense-funded projects and join defense companies as research partners or subcontractors. Inside Talon Secure, researchers can store and work with government information that is unclassified but still must be safeguarded, such as technical data tied to defense programs. The certification confirms the system meets federal requirements for protecting that information. “Protecting sensitive research isn’t a box we check, it’s a standard we hold ourselves to every day,” said Georgia Southern Vice President for Research and Innovation David Weindorf, Ph.D. “This certification opens the door for our faculty to compete for consequential defense research, and it tells our federal partners they can bring that work to Georgia Southern with confidence.” Talon Secure was reviewed by a Certified Third-Party Assessor Organization and earned a perfect score, with no deficiencies in any of the 14 security categories tested. Several Georgia Southern departments collaborated to prepare for the audit, including the Office of Research Integrity, Research Security and Export Controls and Information Technology Services. Janny Crespo-Grow, Ph.D., director of the Office of Research Integrity, said the assessor described Georgia Southern’s performance as “the standard for what we should see in our assessments.” Crespo-Grow, part of the Office of Research Integrity, specifically credited Chief Information Security Officer Nic Carroll and his team, who “took point” in preparation. Carroll highlighted the cross-divisional collaboration behind the audit. “Preparing for the audit meant bringing together people from the Office of Research and Innovation, IT, information security and compliance to answer one honest question: ‘Does what we actually do every day match what our written procedures say we do?’” he said. He added assessors tested 110 security controls against 320 assessment objectives. “The assessment confirmed our protections are followed in practice, not just written down, and that is what gives our researchers an environment they can trust,” Carroll said.

title: Benny G’s Mom, a Breast Cancer Survivor, Emotionally Introduces Him to the Grand Ole Opry Stage on Opry Goes Pink Night - American Songwriter
content: Benny G got a very special introduction to the Grand Ole Opry stage. The singer performed during Opry Goes pink, an annual concert put on in partnership with Susan G. Komen amid Breast Cancer Awareness month. Ahead of Benny’s performance, Opry host Kelly Sutton stepped aside to allow the singer’s mom, breast cancer survivor Ali Goldsmith, to introduce her son. “Five years ago I was diagnosed at the age of 43 with metastatic breast cancer,” Goldsmith began. She went on to shout out the doctors who cared for her amid her illness, before turning the focus to her son. “I believe that every single soul is an entire universe,” she said. “So naturally, there is no greater blessing in my life than the three incredible lights that I refer to as my children.” Goldsmith went to reveal how Benny comforted her during the height of her illness. “When I was ill, he would sit at the edge of my bed with his acoustic guitar and we would sing songs together by many of the artists that performed on this legendary stage,” she said. “It was music and my unwavering faith that gave me both comfort and strength during such a challenging time.” “I want to thank the Grand Ole Opry for shining a bright pink light on this awful disease and also giving me the honor of introducing this next performer,” Goldsmith continued. “This truly is our full circle moment. So with all the joy in my heart, which I refer to is nachas, ladies and gentlemen, let’s give a Grand Ole Opry welcome to my son, Benny G.” “Love you mom, first of all,” he said. “This first song I’m going to play you guys is actually inspired by my mom and her perseverance and faith when she had cancer… It’s called ‘Heaven Knows We Just Keep Dancing Through It All,’ ’cause that’s what life’s about, really.” Next, Benny performed “In the Now,” a song he co-wrote with his sister, Ella Goldsmith. The 19-year-old performer concluded his set by welcoming Briley King back out onto the stage. The pair performed a cover of Marvin Gaye and Tammi Terrell’s “Ain’t No Mountain High Enough.” Benny wasn’t the only star on hand for the special Opry show. Deana Carter opened up the night, and was followed by sets from Mackenzie Carpenter and Megan Moroney. Additionally, Jillian Cardarelli made her Grand Ole Opry debut. Audience members were also treated to solo sets by both King and Mandy Barnett.

title: Freddy Carrick-Smith’s 12th in Sölden Makes British GS History - Ski Racing Media
content: Freddy Carrick-Smith scored his first World Cup points in Sölden, finishing 12th in the 2026/27 men’s season-opening giant slalom. Lucas Pinheiro Braathen won the race with his fourth straight elite giant slalom victory. Carrick-Smith’s result gave Britain its first men’s World Cup GS top 30 since March 2022. Carrick-Smith’s twin brother Zak and elder brother Luca watched from the finish area. His mother, four-time British Olympian Emma Carrick-Anderson, remains his technician and watched from the wings. Freddy’s father, Phil Smith, remains watched from the top. Freddy heard him last before pushing out of the Rettenbach start gate. This wasn’t just Freddy’s first World Cup points result. It also put Britain back on the giant slalom map. His family has worked nearly 20 years for this moment. Speaking exclusively with the Skiing Is Believing podcast less than 24 hours after the race, Carrick-Smith said, “The whole family was there … and we were over the moon after the second run.” This was only Carrick-Smith’s fifth World Cup start and second in Sölden. He made his World Cup debut there 12 months earlier. He finished 54th after the first run, more than 1.6 seconds outside the top 30. Carrick-Smith started with bib 46 and tied Norway’s Hans Grahl-Madsen for 21st after Run 1. “When I saw the 21st on the screen, I was happy and actually snapped my pole while celebrating,” he said. He then produced the fifth-fastest second run and climbed nine places. The course had one speed trap before the final flat, measuring the speed racers carried into the closing stretch. Carrick-Smith posted the fastest reading in Run 1 at 82.20 km/h. His 80.20 km/h in Run 2 ranked second. Carrick-Smith summed up what the result meant to him: “If you don’t enjoy the journey, you’re not going to enjoy the result.” Jeremy Palmer-Tomkinson’s ninth-place finish in Méribel, France, on March 10, 1968, remains Britain’s best men’s World Cup GS result. Carrick-Smith’s 12th was the country’s best in the discipline since then. Charlie Raposo had Britain’s last men’s World Cup GS top 30 before Sölden. He finished 27th in Kranjska Gora on March 12, 2022, then placed 16th the next day. Raposo was in Sölden on Sunday and told Ski Racing Media, “I’m very glad that someone has come along and taken that.” Raposo also praised Carrick-Smith’s skiing and focus between runs: “It was super fun to watch. He was calm, super dialed and super focused between runs so super excited for him.” Carrick-Smith also became the first British man to score World Cup points in Sölden. Chemmy Alcott remains Britain’s top finisher there, placing 10th in 2008. This result means the Carrick-Smith family’s schedule for late November and December now looks a little different. Freddy’s 12th-place finish opened a start opportunity for Zak at the men’s World Cup giant slalom in Copper Mountain, Colorado, on Nov. 29. Before then, Freddy might make his World Cup slalom debut in Levi, Finland, on Nov. 15. Dave Ryding’s retirement after the 2026 Olympic Winter Games could create an opening alongside slalom specialists Laurie Taylor and Billy Major. Freddy and Zak turn 20 in February. The Sölden result gives Freddy a chance, with limited pressure, to leave his footprint in the snow. It could also put two Carrick-Smith brothers on a World Cup start list together. The next generation of British athletes is stepping up to the top level. Whether it’s Freddy, Luca or Zak, the Carrick-Smith name on the World Cup results sheet is one fans may have to get used to. title: NBA Power Rankings: How all 30 teams stack up after one week - ESPN
content:
It has been a little over a week since the start of the 2026-27 NBA regular season, and we've already had a jam-packed couple of days filled with surprise starts, star returns and a few disappointing debuts. LeBron James kicked off his 24th season with the new-look Philadelphia 76ers by defeating the defending champs -- the New York Knicks -- after their ring ceremony at Madison Square Garden and displaying early positive returns following a busy offseason. On the flip side, the San Antonio Spurs, after a Finals appearance in June, are struggling behind young superstar Victor Wembanyama. However, their cross-state rivals, the Houston Rockets, are one of four undefeated teams left in the Western Conference, along with the Oklahoma City Thunder (the 2024-25 champions), the Memphis Grizzlies and the Portland Trail Blazers. In our first iteration of Power Rankings since the campaign started, our NBA insiders break down their biggest observations from opening week, including the most surprising statistic or trend for every team, and what to expect as teams try to find their footing or build on their momentum. Note: Team rankings are based on where members of our panel (ESPN's Jamal Collier, Michael C. Wright, Tim MacMahon, Dave McMenamin, Vincent Goodwill, Zach Kram, Ben Golliver, Kris Rhim and Anthony Slater) think teams belong. Jump to a team:
ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE
DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND
LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN
NO | NY | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX
POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS Next games: @ DAL (Oct. 28), @ HOU (Oct. 31), @ CLE (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: Third-year guard Ajay Mitchell's elevated role. In the wake of the serious injuries suffered by Jalen Williams (fibula/ankle) and Cason Wallace (shoulder), Mitchell should see an increased role on the floor. He has repeatedly shown that he can thrive as the No. 2 offensive option alongside two-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. Mitchell averaged 22.5 points and 6.0 assists in the Thunder's sweep of the Lakers in last season's Western Conference semifinals, when Williams was sidelined. Mitchell had a career-high 30 points and five assists in Monday's win over the Suns, his first start of the season. -- Tim MacMahon Next games: vs. GS (Oct. 28), vs. LAC (Oct. 30), @ SA (Oct. 31), vs. MIL (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 120.8 offensive rating. Anthony Edwards and LaMelo Ball's instant chemistry was marvelous: Minnesota's new-look starting lineup outscored opponents by 31 points in 56 minutes through four games. Meanwhile, the Timberwolves posted a 120.8 offensive rating when their dynamic guard duo shared the court -- an exceptional mark that would have ranked second in the NBA last season. However, that could all come to a halt as Edwards will be sidelined up to two months, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Tuesday, after he undergoes an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee. -- Ben Golliver Next games: vs. CHA (Oct. 28), @ BKN (Oct. 30), @ CHA (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 42%. That's what the previously anemic Pistons have shot from 3 in the first three games this season. Duncan Robinson leads the league in makes per game (5.0) and is shooting a blistering 54% from distance, while newcomer John Collins is taking nearly five a night at a 50% clip. Last season, this team was barely near the league average and struggled at creating and making shots in the playoffs, leading to their second-round loss to Cleveland. Head coach J.B. Bickerstaff said Robinson is more comfortable looking for shots and taking contested ones, which also means some regression to the mean will occur. But being more aggressive is a positive sign of sorts. -- Vincent Goodwill Next games: @ MIL (Oct. 28), @ DAL (Oct. 30), vs. OKC (Oct. 31), vs. BOS (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 4-0 start. For the first time since 2014-15, Houston is off to a 4-0 start and finally playing the way it was expected to last season when it first acquired Kevin Durant. The return of veteran point guard Fred VanVleet, who missed last season with a torn ACL, has played a role in Durant starting off the season with four straight 20-point games for the 10th time in his career. Meanwhile, big man Alperen Sengun is feasting off the order VanVleet has restored to the offense, becoming just the third Rocket to put together multiple 25-5-5 games within the first four games of the season. -- Michael C. Wright Next games: @ IND (Oct. 28), vs. NYK (Oct. 30), @ CHA (Oct. 31), vs. CHI (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 8.8. The Sixers averaged 8.8 offensive rebounds per game. As the Sixers struggled to rebound in the preseason, coach Nick Nurse wasn't concerned. "We're going to be a good rebounding team," he said then. The Sixers still aren't, ranking 29th in the NBA in offensive rebounding per game and 26th in total rebounds per game. The struggles make some sense as the Sixers' front court has been decimated with injury, but it remains concerning and something Nurse is hoping they fix quickly. "I think that our guys understand that we got to do a better job," he said. -- Kris Rhim Next games: @ LAC (Oct. 28), @ GS (Oct. 30), vs. TOR (Nov. 1), vs. MIA (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 60/60/90. Austin Reaves got off to an unbelievably hot start through the Lakers' 3-0 showing out of the gates, averaging a career-best 26.7 points on 63.9% from the field, 61.5% from 3 and 89.7% from the free throw line entering Tuesday's game. He and Luka Doncic (34.3 points per game) are the only pair of teammates in the top 10 in scoring in the league. They would be even more effective if they took care of the ball better. They also both rank in the top 10 in turnovers per game through three games, with 7.0 for Doncic and 4.3 for Reaves. -- Dave McMenamin Next games: vs. ORL (Oct. 28), vs. ORL (Oct. 30), @ LAL (Nov. 1), @ LAC (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 0-12. The Raptors' only loss this season came with Kawhi Leonard sidelined, but Toronto will be without Leonard for a period of weeks as he manages left knee soreness. The concerning part about life without Leonard is that in the Raptors' first look without him, Scottie Barnes had one of the worst outings of his career, finishing 0-12 with three turnovers and a team-worst minus-27 in the 117-94 loss. -- Rhim Next games: vs. CHI (Oct. 30), @ ORL (Nov. 1), @ HOU (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: Jordan Walsh is in the starting lineup. Starting Walsh, a rotational player who started 25 games last season, came as a bit of a surprise with veterans such as Sam Hauser and Payton Pritchard on the roster. But so far, Walsh's defense has buoyed the Celtics early in the season, slowing down guards including the Knicks' Jalen Brunson (2-for-7, five points against Walsh) and the Pistons' Cade Cunningham (1-for-3, three points against Walsh), according to NBA.com. -- Rhim Next games: @ UTAH (Oct. 28), vs. MIN (Oct. 31), vs. UTAH (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 0-2 start. The Spurs ran into the combustible mixture of growing pains in trying to evolve their offense with a new starting five while facing two of the West's toughest teams -- Oklahoma City and Houston -- to start the season. So, the early struggles weren't unexpected, and the Spurs are comfortable with taking their lumps early. But in the process of trying to raise its ceiling, San Antonio lowered its floor, a disturbing early trend. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said, "We've got to just keep getting back to the standard we know we are capable of. Our floor right now is way too low." -- Wright Next games: vs. MEM (Oct. 29), @ UTAH (Oct. 31), @ DEN (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 21-0 lead. The Blazers enjoyed the perfect start to the intriguing Damian Lillard and Ja Morant partnership thanks to a blowout win over the Suns in their season opener. Portland raced out to a 21-0 lead in front of a raucous Moda Center crowd that eagerly welcomed Lillard back from an Achilles injury. Though Morant opened the season as a starter, he has had to make great sacrifices to fit into Portland's crowded backcourt rotation. The two-time All-Star is tracking toward career lows in minutes, points, shots and usage rate. -- Golliver Next games: vs. PHI (Oct. 28), @ MIA (Oct. 30), vs. BKN (Nov. 1), vs. ATL (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 21.8. The number of points Tyrese Haliburton is averaging through his first four games back from injury. He has scored at least 20 in three of the first four games of a season for only the second time in his career, played in a back-to-back this week and he's averaging 9.5 assists. Any worries about him needing to ease back into action have been unfounded. Haliburton looks like his old self after missing 16 months, but the Pacers are going to need to get healthier around him. (Ivica Zubac has a sprained left ankle, T.J. McConnell has yet to play in a game in either preseason or regular season and Ben Sheppard tore his meniscus.) -- Jamal Collier Next games: @ NO (Oct. 28), @ PHX (Oct. 30), vs. POR (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: The Nuggets' 119.3 defensive rating is fifth worst in the league. It's been a strange first homestand for the Nuggets. They fell 23 points to the Pelicans and even received some boos, but then stormed back for an overtime win with help from rookie Trevon Brazile, who made a handful of spectacular plays and looks like a second-round steal at a time Denver desperately needs depth. After the game, Nikola Jokic called out the jeering fans, saying they weren't welcome back, and doubled down a couple of nights later after they were blown out at home by the previously winless Warriors. -- Anthony Slater Next games: vs. WAS (Oct. 28), @ ATL (Oct. 29), @ MIL (Oct. 31), vs. OKC (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: Keep an eye on the wing trio of Peyton Watson, Sam Merrill and Jaylon Tyson and how they complement Cleveland's core four throughout the season. That trio has made just 19.5% of their combined 3-pointers so far -- but it's still very early, so there's plenty of time for those role players to turn it around and start making more shots in support of the stars. -- Zach Kram Wednesday, Nov. 4

• Mavericks-Spurs, 9:30 p.m. ET Wednesday, Nov. 11
• Cavaliers-Knicks, 7 p.m. ET
• Warriors-Rockets, 9:30 p.m. ET Next games: @ POR (Oct. 29), vs. SAC (Oct. 31), vs. NO (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: Ty Jerome's hot start and the Grizzlies 4-0 start. Memphis' 4-0 start ranks as the second best in franchise history behind the 2014-15 campaign in which the Grizzlies won their first six games. Perhaps the most eye-popping early trend comes from the way this young team has performed in clutch time. Three of Memphis' first four outings turned out to be clutch-time games, with the Grizzlies winning all of them to tie the 76ers for the most clutch wins so far this season. Jerome ranks third in the league in scoring (29.8 points per game) after a career-high 45-point season opener, which he then followed with 31 points against the Kings. -- Wright Next games: vs. MIA (Oct. 28), vs. CLE (Oct. 29), @ NO (Oct. 31), @ IND (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: Can Quin Snyder continue to rely heavily on his rotation? One storyline entering the season was whether the Hawks' frontcourt could succeed against quality opponents. The loss at Houston proved they have a long way to go. In the 10-point loss, Atlanta was outrebounded 40-22 on the offensive glass (52-35 overall) and were minus-11 in free-throw attempts. The lone frontcourt player with a positive plus-minus was Onyeka Okongwu. Through the first four games, nine players have averaged more than 18 MPG, with only starter Jalen Johnson averaging more than 30 MPG. -- Bobby Marks Next games: @ CHI (Oct. 28), @ PHI (Oct. 30), vs. BKN (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 30th. That's where the Knicks ranked in both offensive efficiency and raw scoring entering Tuesday's game. It's a small sample size, but the Knicks have barely shown more than flashes of that potent offense. "We get a little comfortable," Jalen Brunson said after Sunday's loss to Orlando, in which New York gave up 40 fourth-quarter points to the Magic. Before Tuesday, Mikal Bridges registered donuts at the foul line and 3-point line. One is expected, the other is not. -- Goodwill Next games: @ DET (Oct. 28), @ WAS (Oct. 30), vs. PHI (Oct. 31), vs. DET (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 36.3 PPG. New Hornets Grayson Allen and Naz Reid came to Charlotte in trades for Miles Bridges and LaMelo Ball, respectively, and both sharpshooters are excelling in their new digs. Allen and Reid have combined to average 36.3 points per game while making 44% of their 3-pointers, and both players rank in the top 10 in the NBA in made 3s. -- Kram Next games: @ CLE (Oct. 28), vs. CHA (Oct. 30), @ ORL (Nov. 2 Most surprising stat or trend: 8.8 PPG. After averaging 16.3 points per game with a 26% usage rate in a promising sophomore season, Alex Sarr is down to 8.8 PPG with a 14% usage rate this year. That decline epitomizes the difficult balancing act for the Wizards as they try to win games with veteran stars Trae Young and Anthony Davis, while also providing opportunities for their many prospects to develop on the court. -- Kram Most surprising stat or trend: 40. Devin Booker recorded the 40th 40-point game of his career with 43 points on 17-of-25 shooting in the Suns' 131-122 win over the Warriors opening week. It's the most in franchise history, with Amar'e Stoudemire trailing significantly behind at No. 2 with 15 of them. Phoenix is off to a slow start, however, with Booker combining for just 26 points on 8-of-20 shooting in the Suns' other two losses. -- McMenamin Next games: @ TOR (Oct. 28), @ TOR (Oct. 30), vs. BOS (Nov. 1), vs. WAS (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 3. Injuries are forcing Orlando to utilize its third starting lineup in four games when it plays Toronto on Wednesday. Former All-Star Paolo Banchero is out indefinitely with an ankle injury, while Jalen Suggs will miss at least two weeks due to a bone bruise in his right knee. Injuries have impacted them in the past two seasons, with Banchero and Franz Wagner playing only 64 games together in that span. -- Marks ESPN Analytics has unveiled its new NBA Trade Lab, an interactive web app for fans to build, save and vote on mock trades. Utah's frontcourt has been ravaged by injuries, as Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee), Lauri Markkanen (wrist) and Jusuf Nurkic (toe) are all sidelined. Second-year forward Bailey's performance has been a silver lining during the Jazz's rough start. Bailey, the No. 5 pick in last year's draft, has back-to-back double-doubles, averaging 17 points, 11 rebounds, 3.5 assists and two blocks in the two games. -- MacMahon Next games: vs. OKC (Oct. 28), vs. HOU (Oct. 30), vs. SAC (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: Cooper Flagg's disruptive abilities. Flagg's disruptive defensive tendencies were as much of a factor as his offensive potential in scouts and executives considering him one of the best draft prospects in a generation and those skills have been on display early this season. Flagg leads the league with 3.7 steals per game and ranks in the top 20 in blocks (1.7). He had five steals and three blocks during his 29-point, 11-assist masterpiece in Monday's win in Miami. The only other teens to ever record at least five steals and three blocks in a game: Kevin Garnett and Wembanyama, both of whom went on to win a Defensive Player of the Year award. -- MacMahon Next games: vs. LAL (Oct. 28), @ MIN (Oct. 30), @ GS (Nov. 1), vs. TOR (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 26.3%. That is Rui Hachimura's field goal percentage through his first three games with the Clippers after signing a two-year, $28 million contract to move from Crypto.com Arena to the Intuit Dome in the offseason. The dip in efficiency comes off a season when he shot 51.4% for the Lakers -- the second-best clip of his career -- and raised his level to 54.9% in the playoffs. Hachimura had only 11 games last season out of the 68 he played where he shot under 30% for the game. He has done that in two out of his first three games with the Clippers. -- McMenamin Next games: @ ATL (Oct. 28), vs. IND (Oct. 30), @ LAL (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 105.3. On opening night, Giddey revealed he injured his left wrist and will have to manage the injury all season. Both his production -- 7.0 points and 7.3 assists on 33% shooting -- and playing time have dipped as a result, and the Bulls offense has sputtered out of the gates. Entering Tuesday, they had the worst offensive rating in the league through four games. -- Collier Next games: vs. DEN (Oct. 28), vs. SAC (Oct. 29), vs. ATL (Oct. 31), @ MEM (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: 23-point collapse. Jamahl Mosley is still seeking his first win as coach after New Orleans inexplicably blew a 23-point lead to Denver on Saturday. The Pelicans might regret their stumbles out of the gate: The NBA handed them a soft early-season schedule, playing nine of their first 13 games against teams that missed the 2026 playoffs. Mosley has started 2025 lottery pick Jeremiah Fears, but the guard's abysmal shooting -- 29% from the field and 18.2% from deep -- has been a real drag on the Pelicans' offense. -- Golliver Download the ESPN app and enable Shams Charania's news alerts to receive push notifications for the latest updates first. Next games: @ MIN (Oct. 28), vs. LAL (Oct. 30), vs. LAC (Nov. 1), vs. PHX (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: It couldn't have been a louder opening week to a career for Yaxel Lendeborg. After getting in a public dustup with Doncic (they face each other again on Friday), the rookie wing went on a statistical binge, becoming the fourth player since 1986 to compile at least 85 points and 35 rebounds in his first four games. Shaquille O'Neal, Patrick Ewing and David Robinson are the other three. It didn't take long for him to earn Steve Kerr's trust. Lendeborg put away the Nuggets on Monday night with Stephen Curry on the bench and Kerr said afterward, "He's going to be a guy who closes games." -- Slater Next games: vs. HOU (Oct. 28), vs. CLE (Oct. 31), @ MIN (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: Zero. That's the number of minutes Gary Trent Jr. has played for the Bucks this season despite signing a four-year, $64 million contract during the offseason. At least Milwaukee has avoided having a zero in the win column after a win against Indiana on Monday, dodging what would have been the Bucks' first 0-4 start in 50 years. -- Collier Next games: vs. DET (Oct. 30), @ IND (Nov. 1), @ NYK (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: Julius Randle has been efficient, despite the losses. He kept them in their first two games -- which were respectable losses to Charlotte and Cleveland -- and led them to an overtime loss against the Celtics on Tuesday night. He leads the Nets in scoring (22.0), rebounding (7.0) and assists (6.3) while shooting over 50% from the field and 45% from 3. For a team that will struggle to score all season, having Randle play aggressively will at least keep this young team in games.  -- Goodwill Next games: @ NO (Oct. 29), @ MEM (Oct. 31), @ DAL (Nov. 2) Most surprising stat or trend: As expected, rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. has received the greenest of lights. title: BMW F 450 GS Trophy Edition: Big GS Energy, A Few Growing Pains - Man's World India
content: The smallest GS has grown up, gained a second cylinder, and learned to operate its own clutch. But is that enough to justify its premium price tag? For a long time, the G 310 GS was the cheapest way into the GS family in India. The F 450 GS replaces it, and it is a different kind of motorcycle. It has a new 420cc parallel twin, and the top variant, the Trophy Edition, also gets the Easy Ride Clutch. BMW launched the Trophy at ₹5.30 lakh ex-showroom in April. In September, the price went up by ₹30,000, so it now costs ₹5.60 lakh. I have spent some time with it, and I mostly like it. The engine is the one part I am still trying to figure out. I like the design. It reminds me of the older GS siblings, with the beak, the flyline and the tall stance. The X-shaped headlamp comes from the R 1300 GS, and the Trophy's Racing Blue with red and white accents suits it well. It also gets you a lot of attention. A lot of people asked me what bike it is, and how much it costs. The answer to that is ₹5.60 lakh ex-showroom. It looks heavy, but it doesn't feel heavy at all. BMW says the kerb weight is 178 kg, and the bike is very well balanced. I am 183 cm tall, and I was able to flat-foot it on the 845 mm seat. It is a fairly large motorcycle, though. In traffic, you have to be careful while manoeuvring it in tight spaces. The Trophy gets BMW's Easy Ride Clutch, or ERC. It is a centrifugal clutch that engages after roughly 2,500 to 2,700 rpm, so you can move off and come to a stop without using the clutch lever. You still change gears yourself, and the Trophy also gets a quickshifter. It takes some time to get used to. The feeling of not using the clutch is a bit uncanny at first. But it works well, and the bike doesn't stall. And if you don't want to leave it to the system, you can take over manual control with the lever at any time. The suspension is really good. The Trophy gets the sport setup, which means a 43 mm KYB upside-down fork with adjustable compression and rebound, and a rear monoshock with travel-dependent damping. Both ends have 180 mm of travel. It is slightly on the stiffer side, and I like it that way. Heavier riders may like it even more. The 420cc parallel twin makes 48 hp at 8,750 rpm and 43 Nm at 6,750 rpm. BMW says 80 per cent of that torque is available from 3,000 rpm, and the engine does have great pull. It stays very refined till about 80 to 90 kmph. Once you start pushing it, you can feel the engine working. I was able to push it past 120 kmph, but it felt a little stressed at that point. The character is the part I find hard to describe. It is not very refined, even though it is a twin and it carries a BMW badge. But it is also not as characterful or as frantic as the 390 Adventure. It sits somewhere in a strange, boring middle. BMW has gone with an unusual 135-degree crank on this engine. The idea is to keep vibrations in check and give it a throaty sound, but I would not call the result either refined or exciting. The saddle is quite nice, for both the rider and the pillion. The brakes are good and bitey, with a 310 mm disc at the front. This is the part I find bizarre. At ₹5.60 lakh ex-showroom, the bike gets a 6.5-inch TFT, riding modes that change the throttle response, and heated grips as standard. But there is no Hill Hold Control and no cruise control. Without Hill Hold Control, the bike can roll back when you stop on a slope, and there is no parking brake either. Reviewers have also found that leaving the bike in gear on an incline doesn't reliably hold it in place. That feels like an odd gap on a bike that is built to make starting and stopping easier. Cruise control is not offered even as an optional extra, which is a miss on a bike that is meant for long distances. There is a lot to like here. The design, the balance, the suspension, the saddle and the brakes are all good, and the ERC works well once you get used to it. The engine is where it doesn't quite make up its mind. It pulls well and stays refined in the first half of its range, but it is not as smooth as I would expect from a BMW twin, and it is not as exciting as the 390 Adventure. At ₹5.60 lakh ex-showroom, that is hard to overlook, and the missing Hill Hold Control and cruise control make it harder. If you want a light, good-looking GS that is comfortable for two, this does the job well. Just know what you are getting with the engine.

title: GS Affiliate Energy Materials Suspends Operations Amid Financial Woes, Pursues Sale - 아시아경제

GS Affiliate Energy Materials Suspends Operations Amid Financial Woes, Pursues Sale GS E&C's waste battery recycling subsidiary Energy Materials has halted operations at its factory amid financial difficulties. Losses have mounted due to difficulties securing raw materials and falling prices for recovered metals, and the company is pursuing a sale after undertaking restructuring measures, including offering voluntary retirement. Energy Materials, a secondary battery recycling company in Pohang, North Gyeongsang Province. Yonhap News Agency According to industry sources, Energy Materials suspended operations at its factory in Pohang, North Gyeongsang Province, on October 28. It is also offering voluntary retirement to its more than 130 employees. Founded in October 2020, Energy Materials has extracted battery metals, including lithium, nickel, cobalt, and manganese, from black powder, a black substance obtained by shredding and heat-treating waste batteries. Despite large-scale investment in facilities, the factory's operating rate remained at around 30%. Because of the time lag between the adoption of electric vehicles and the eventual disposal of their batteries, the company could not secure enough feedstock for processing. The decline in selling prices for recovered metals further worsened profitability. With the factory operating at a low rate, the company continued to bear fixed costs for facilities and personnel, and its cumulative losses reached about 170 billion won. The company pursued cost reductions, workforce efficiency measures, diversification of raw-material suppliers and product buyers, and efforts to attract new investors, but was unable to overcome its financial difficulties. Challenges in the battery recycling industry are also continuing overseas.
